findings.title: parseQuantity does not validate input, allowing NaN to corrupt cart totals
findings.problem: parseQuantity uses parseInt(text) with no radix argument and no validation of the result. If the customer-supplied text is not a valid integer (e.g. empty string, 'abc', or a decimal like '2.5'), parseInt returns NaN or a truncated value with no error raised. There is no check for NaN, negative numbers, or zero.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate the parsed result: use Number.isInteger checks after parseInt(text, 10), reject or clamp NaN/negative/zero values, and throw or return an explicit error for invalid input rather than silently propagating NaN.

findings.title: No test coverage for session.js and most of cart.js exports
findings.problem: The only test file present exercises just the `subtotal` function. `applyDiscount` and `parseQuantity` in cart.js, and all exported functions in session.js (`createSession`, `isExpired`, `refresh`, including the expiry boundary behavior), have no automated tests.
findings.recommendedFix: Add unit tests for applyDiscount (including rounding edge cases), parseQuantity, createSession, isExpired (boundary at exact expiresAt), and refresh (including the throw path).
